title: Weekly pilot sync - prefix reuse & KV tuning
summary: Review of week 2 pilot metrics: prefix cache hit rate improvements after normalization and prompt canonicalization; discussion on KV vs prefix granularity, eviction policy, and plan for incremental A/B rollout. Action items assigned for instrumentation, PRs, and one-week 30% traffic test to measure latency & cost impact.
action_items: Priya - add prefix fingerprinting hook to inference path (PR) - due 2025-11-07
Samir - provide 5 canonical prompt templates and examples of user prompt variance - due 2025-11-06
Marcus - enable KV cache metrics in infra stack and forward to Redwood dashboard - due 2025-11-09
Jamie - share updated cost calc spreadsheet and A/B plan - due 2025-11-05
next_steps: Run 1-week A/B with 30% traffic on prefix-normalization enabled
Instrument per-key hit/miss and latency breakdown (p50/p95) in dashboard
Merge fingerprinting PR after lightweight load test
Re-evaluate eviction TTL to 2h with LRU policy after A/B results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-04 15:00 PT | Duration: ~38m | Recording: yes | Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Solstice), Hannah (Solstice PM), Marcus (Solstice Infra), Olga (Solstice Privacy)

[00:00:01] Jamie: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync, uh this is Jamie from Redwood. How are we doing Samir?

[00:00:10] Samir: Hey yeah good, uh just finished a quick spin on the new prefix normalizer you pushed last night, saw some numbers I wanna dig into.

[00:00:18] Priya: awesome, quick agenda: run through this weeks metrics, go over the KV vs prefix granularity proposals, talk eviction/TTL, then agree next steps. Sound good?

[00:00:30] Hannah: yep sounds good to me.

[00:00:35] Jamie: cool, Priya you wanna start with the metrics slide? I posted a short sheet in the chat, link is in the notes.

[00:00:42] Priya: yep, ok so week 2 baseline: before our canonicalization we were seeing prefix hit rates around 28% across the sample traffic, after the lightweight normalization and a small de-dup pass the hit rate bumped to 46% on the same sample window. That's aggregated across sessions, so some routes are much higher and some lower. The median per-route hit went from 22% to 41%.

[00:01:10] Marcus: wait can you repeat the 46% number? That seems higher than we expected, are we sure it's not double counting?

[00:01:16] Priya: yeah we double-checked the instrumentation - it's prefix-level dedupe + whitespace normalization + lower-casing for english tokens. We excluded session-specific tokens like user ids. The increase is real but there's variance, the 95th percentile route hit is only 68%, some low frequency routes are still <10%.

[00:01:33] Samir: got it. We were worried about false positives where two different prompts normalize to same prefix, any risk of semantic collisions?

[00:01:40] Priya: good question. We added a quick heuristic where if prompts differ in length by >40% or if they include disjoint entity lists we skip normalization. It isn't perfect but so far low false matches. We can add a stronger hash-based fingerprint.

[00:01:55] Hannah: can you explain the fingerprint idea?

[00:01:58] Priya: yeah, essentially compute a small rolling hash of the canonicalized tokens — think 64-bit fingerprint — attach that to the prefix key, and only treat matches as hit if fingerprint equal. That reduces collision risk dramatically. Overhead is negligible.

[00:02:15] Marcus: what's overhead "negligible" mean? CPU or latency numbers?

[00:02:19] Priya: in our microbench it was ~0.7ms p50 additional CPU on the inference path for fingerprint calc, p95 ~1.6ms. We can do it off critical path for some routes, or sample it initially.

[00:02:30] Jamie: and that ties to cost — with hit rate moving 28%->46% our token spend projection drops roughly 18% in the sheet; we estimate latency improvement p95 around 90-120ms for cached responses because we avoid model exec.

[00:02:45] Samir: nice. Our concern is more about cache pollution: we saw a bunch of very long instruction-heavy prompts that rarely repeat, they push out useful entries. Thoughts on eviction?

[00:02:55] Priya: eviction is key, right now we used an LRU with a TTL window of 1h. For this workload we recommend switching to LRU + size-weighting where longer KV entries cost more, and bump TTL to 2h for higher reuse while aging low-frequency keys faster.

[00:03:12] Marcus: size-weighting makes sense. How do we measure impact?

[00:03:16] Priya: we need per-key hit counters and weighted evictions exposed to your infra metrics. Marcus, you mentioned enabling KV metrics?

[00:03:22] Marcus: yes we can export Prom metrics but need the key-length bucketing from Redwood side. I'll take that on.

[00:03:28] Olga: one privacy note — anything stored in KV or prefix cache still counts as derived user content, we need encryption at rest and audit logs. Do you have KMS integration?

[00:03:36] Jamie: yes we do; for the private pilot we can use your KMS or our managed envelope keys. We also keep an audit trail of cache writes/evictions — low-cardinality metadata only, not full prompt payload unless you opt-in.

[00:03:48] Olga: ok please add a short doc on dataflow for cache writes.

[00:03:52] Jamie: will do.

[00:03:55] Priya: back to tuning — another lever is prompt canonicalization depth. Right now we normalize whitespace, punctuation, and variable masking of emails/ids. We can be more aggressive: remove salutations, strip trailing clarifying phrases, or conversely be more conservative on legal language. There is tradeoff between hit rate and correctness.

[00:04:14] Samir: any examples of where over-normalization broke things?

[00:04:17] Priya: short example: a support prompt like 'Rewrite email to be apologetic' vs 'Rewrite email to be apologetic but terse' — if we strip modifiers we might return a terser tone than desired. So we mark certain tokens as modifiers and preserve them.

[00:04:31] Hannah: ok so we need a whitelist/blacklist of tokens to preserve per-route. Can the system do route-level config?

[00:04:37] Jamie: yes per-route canonicalization policy is supported in the pilot config. We'll surface route config in the console.

[00:04:44] Marcus: about A/B, what's the recommended traffic split? We want minimal risk but measurable effect.

[00:04:48] Priya: recommend 30% traffic on the normalized + fingerprinted cache, 70% control for one week. If numbers look good we widen. We'll also keep canary fallbacks to hosted model variant if cache misses surge.

[00:05:01] Samir: do we need to change client SDK?

[00:05:04] Jamie: no client change needed; this is server-side inference path only. If you want to opt into local pre-hashing we can provide a helper lib but not required.

[00:05:13] Hannah: what are the key metrics we'll watch?

[00:05:15] Priya: prefix hit rate, KV hit rate, per-route latency p50/p95, token spend delta, cache eviction rate, and collisions flagged by fingerprint mismatches. We'll create a dashboard tile for each.

[00:05:26] Marcus: also need a slow path alert if p95 latency increases >10% on control.

[00:05:30] Jamie: noted. Priya can you draft the dashboard layout and share?

[00:05:33] Priya: yes I'll drop a mock in the drive and link it.

[00:05:36] Samir: one more question — is KV cache persisted across restarts? We had a node recycle last week and lost warm cache.

[00:05:42] Priya: by default KV is in-memory with optional persistence to a backing store (rocksdb/s3 snapshot). For the pilot we can enable periodic snapshotting to minimize cold starts. Marcus, any ops concerns?

[00:05:52] Marcus: we'll need to size the snapshot store and plan an RPO, but yes we can enable it for the test.

[00:05:58] Olga: compliance-wise snapshots need to be encrypted and have retention rules. I'll coordinate with Jamie for required retention window.

[00:06:05] Jamie: great. Let's run through concrete timeline and owners. Priya: fingerprinting PR?

[00:06:10] Priya: I'll open a small PR that adds the 64-bit fingerprint and a flag to toggle it per-route. I'll keep it behind a feature flag for canary. Estimated ready by Friday 11/7 after a lightweight bench.

[00:06:21] Jamie: Samir, you said you'd assemble canonical prompt templates?

[00:06:24] Samir: yes I'll pull five high-volume templates and a set of 8-10 noisy variations so you can see real-world delta, target 11/6.

[00:06:31] Marcus: I'll put the metrics export live and add key-length buckets, target 11/9.

[00:06:36] Jamie: I'll share the A/B plan and cost model spreadsheet 11/5. Also I'll attach the security note about cache dataflow.

[00:06:43] Hannah: timeline works for us. Anything else?

[00:06:47] Priya: quick note: in initial runs we measured median end-to-end inference latency drop from ~420ms to ~310ms for cache hits, and overall token spend reduction ~18% — numbers in the sheet. Keep expectations measured for rare routes.

[00:06:59] Samir: cool. If A/B shows >40% hit rate improvement and cost down >12% we'd push to 60% traffic next week.

[00:07:06] Jamie: sounds like a plan. We'll reconvene same time next week to review the week-3 A/B results.

[00:07:12] Olga: one last ask — please CC legal on the dataflow doc.

[00:07:15] Jamie: will do. Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

[00:07:20] End of recording.

Notes/links shared in chat: https://drive.redwood.example/solstice-prefix-pilot (metrics sheet), https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-prs/pull/128 (fingerprint PR - forthcoming), security/dataflow-summary.pdf
